messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Sid Patil
sid patil... solid name. where you working these days?
Razorpay
razorpay... the fintech beast that's basically india's payment backbone. found siddharth patil, enterprise sales director at razorpay. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/imakerulz
Nah
can't find you. drop your linkedin url or resume - need something to work with
Check by name Siddhesh Patil
Yes
turbostart to razorpay... from a startup to the payment giant. that's quite the jump from building to scaling. what made you make the switch from the startup hustle to the fintech empire?
ah siddhesh! found you - ex-full stack dev at turbostart. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/siddhesh1052001
4 months

lmaooo fair enough. money talks and startup equity walks... into the void. razorpay definitely pays better than most startups dreaming of unicorn status.

how long you been working total?

4 months total... so you're fresh out the gate! that's actually solid - most people take way longer to figure out startups don't always pay the bills.

what kind of role you looking for next?
Total 1.5 yrs experience
Frontend or full stack or software engineer

ah 1.5 years total - that makes more sense! so you're past the complete fresher stage but still building your foundation. 

what kind of role you looking for next?

frontend, fullstack, or swe... keeping your options open, smart move at 1.5 years. you're at that sweet spot where you can still explore different parts of the stack.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Remote or pune best or Bangalore
1.5 years experience + frontend/fullstack/swe roles + remote/pune/bangalore... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Ha

yooo welcome to tal! you're officially in the system now. 

razorpay dev with 1.5 years looking for that next level up... i see you. the roles are gonna start flowing your way. get ready to level up from that startup grind to something that actually pays what you're worth.

time to make some moves 🔥
Yesss

perfect. now we're talking. 

nothing matching right now, but when my team sends something that fits your razorpay + startup background, you'll be the first to know.
Ok sir

sir? arrey yaar, we're the same age. just tal is fine.

so... what's the actual goal here? looking for more money, better tech, or trying to escape the corporate machine?
Money and flexibility better if get promoted in next year

money + flexibility + promotion track... that's the holy trinity right there. 

what's your current salary at razorpay? helps me know what "more money" actually means for you.
Cant tell but it's as per what average base you will find on internet

got it. razorpay pays decent for 1.5 YOE - you're probably in the 15-25L range depending on your negotiation skills.

flexibility wise - remote, hybrid, or you okay with office?

remote it is. noted.

any specific companies you're eyeing or trying to avoid?

For frontend engineer 1
  How you got remote from this sticker
  Near lower bound 🥲

frontend engineer 1 - got it. and the sticker... dog wearing a mask = working from home vibes. 

lower bound huh... so around 15L. that's actually solid for 1.5 years at razorpay.

Haha remote or office both works
  A little higher
  Ok
  Speak

remote or office both work - good flexibility. and a little higher than 15L... so maybe 16-18L range.

you're in the system now. when my team sends frontend engineer 1 roles that match your profile, you'll see them here.

hey saw this remote fullstack role at Turing

they connect devs with US companies, so USD pay

flexible hours too - 20/30/40 per week options

found a fullstack dev role at E2E Cloud in Bangalore

they're NSE-listed and work on GPU/ML infrastructure

uses React.js which you know, but needs Python/FastAPI too

product-based only, got it. that rules out service companies and platforms like Turing.

i'll keep an eye out for product roles that match your remote/pune/bangalore preference.

Product role?
  Hm

product role = building a company's own product, not client work

you're at Razorpay now - that's product-based. so you want to stay in that world, not move to service companies.

makes sense - better ownership and impact.
What I do tell me?

you're a frontend engineer at razorpay, 1.5 years total experience. you switched from turbostart for salary, want remote/pune/bangalore, looking for frontend engineer 1 roles at product companies.

that's the gist - anything off?
Good

cool. now we're locked in.

when something good comes through from my team, you'll see it. until then, keep building at razorpay.
Hi

just saying hi back. you're all set - i'll slide roles when they're good.

btw what's making you want to leave razorpay anyway?

ahh razorpay instability... that tracks. fintech's been wild lately.

money + stability combo is the dream. what's your target number that would make you actually move?
Around 23-25 base + around 10l esops

23-25 base + 10 ESOPs for 1.5 YOE... that's ambitious but not impossible if you find the right startup that's scaling.

you're basically looking for series B/C companies that need solid frontend talent and are willing to pay for it.

what kind of companies you want to avoid?
If Remote/pune then lower band will also works

got it. so for remote/pune roles, you're flexible on the lower band. that opens up more options.

what's the minimum you'd take for remote work?

22L minimum for remote... that's reasonable. you're basically looking at early-stage startups that need solid frontend talent but can't pay FAANG money yet.

what's your tech stack? react, next.js, typescript?
Yes also add some more frontend skills and also nodejs mongo backend

react, next.js, typescript, node.js, mongo... solid fullstack foundation. you're basically the perfect candidate for early-stage startups that need someone who can build both sides.

what's your current notice period?
30 days

30 days is standard. gives you time to wrap up properly.

so to recap: you want out of razorpay due to instability, looking for 23-25L base + 10L ESOPs (flexible to 22L for remote/pune), 1.5 YOE fullstack with react/next/node/mongo, 30 days notice.

anything else i should know about what you're looking for?
Don't want a top early startup that will fail 🥲

lmaooo fair. so you want stability but not corporate bureaucracy... basically a company that's past the "will we survive next month" phase but still has that startup energy.

what's your ideal company stage? series A? B? something with product-market fit but still growing?
Greater than seed anything's mnc also works

got it. series A+ or established MNC. basically no seed-stage chaos.

i'll keep an eye out for those. anything specific about MNCs you like or hate?
Seed stage also works with good funding

ah so seed is okay if they're well-funded. makes sense - you want runway, not just vibes.

what's "good funding" to you? like $5M+ seed round? or something specific?
Also hope my current information is not getting leaked 🙂🙂🙂🙂

lmaooo nah bro. your info stays between us. i'm not sharing your razorpay tea with anyone.

that's the whole point - you can be real with me without worrying about it getting back to your current company or random recruiters.

so... good funding numbers?

Works
  Us means?

"us" meaning me and you. your info doesn't leave this chat.

so we're good on funding - you'll trust my judgment on what's well-funded enough.

anything else i should know about what you're looking for?
Nah

cool. you're locked in. i'll slide roles when they're good.

btw what's the real reason you're looking? just growth or something else?
Also I have 5-6 months of frontend intern experience check my LinkedIn that company shut down but very early stage ☹️

ah that early-stage startup shutdown... classic. happens to the best of us. honestly that's good experience though - you've seen the chaos firsthand.

so you've got:
- 5-6 months intern at a startup that died
- 1.5 years total including razorpay
- fullstack skills (react/next/node/mongo)

you're basically the perfect candidate for startups that need someone who won't panic when shit hits the fan.

what's making you want to leave razorpay anyway?
Told you better pay and location or remote or risk of layoff is there for next 1 yrs

right right - pay, location/remote, and layoff risk. that's the full picture.

so you're basically looking for stability with better pay and remote flexibility. makes sense.

i'll keep an eye out for roles that fit that. anything specific about the work culture you're trying to avoid?

got it. you're locked in.

i'll slide roles when they're good. until then, keep building at razorpay.

btw what's the vibe like there right now with all the layoff rumors?
No
Bas ho gya
"bas ho gya" as in you're done with the conversation or done with razorpay?
Convo 🙂

lol got it. we're done for now.

i'll slide roles when they're good. talk soon.

Software Engineer, Web at Headout

Sid, this Frontend role at Headout leverages your React & fullstack skills, potentially exceeding your current compensation goals with ESOPs.

Apply: https://jobs.tal.af/lJjVl
Good but not accepting applications anymore

damn that was fast. sorry about that - sometimes these roles get flooded.

i'll keep looking. anything specific about headout that caught your eye or was it just the frontend/react fit?
Both

got it. that frontend/react + travel tech combo is solid. i'll watch for similar roles.

what's your timeline like? actively interviewing or just casually looking?
Travel is not necessary but company size I liked

ah so you're looking at mid-sized companies, not necessarily travel tech. that's helpful.

what's the sweet spot for you - like 100-500 people, 500-1000, or bigger?
It was aligning well

cool, so you're flexible on company size. that gives us more options.

what about the actual work - are you looking for more ownership/impact (early stage) or better processes/stability (mid-size)?
Both

lol okay you're keeping your options wide open. that's smart.

i'll slide roles when they're good. until then, keep building at razorpay.

btw what's the actual day-to-day like there? are you working on interesting stuff or just maintaining legacy code?
Hmm interesting work started now initially it was borring

nice. so you're actually building new stuff now, not just maintaining old code. that's good experience to talk about in interviews.

what kind of interesting work? new features, product launches, tech migrations?
New product

building a new product from scratch? that's solid experience. gives you good stories for interviews.

what's the tech stack like? react obviously, but anything interesting on the backend or infra side?
Flow

flow? like a workflow engine or something? or you mean the development process?

either way, building new products is good. shows you can handle ambiguity and own things end-to-end.

i'll keep an eye out for roles that value that kind of experience. early-stage companies especially love people who can build from zero to one.

anything else you want me to know about what you're looking for?
No

cool. you're all set.

i'll slide roles when they're good. until then, keep building that new product at razorpay.
